plain: The podcast host Jesse Michels passes on a story first told by Mark McCandlish, an illustrator of aircraft. According to it, in 1988 a man named Brad Sorensen was shown three bell- or acorn-shaped craft, called flux liners or alien reproduction vehicles, meaning human-built copies of alien craft, and they looked worn as if they had been flown. The story places this at Palmdale, California, though some tellers put it at an air show at Norton Air Force Base. A researcher known as UAPGerb says he believes the story, calls the craft a copycat vehicle, and adds that in 1990 Sorensen admitted it to Bill Scott, an editor at the aviation magazine Aviation Week. If true, it would mean the US had already built working copies of alien technology.
